[1/4] Cycle 6: give Hint, Undo and Reset distinct audio cues instead of the shared 660Hz tick, so blind and glance-away players can tell what changed; prove with unit frequency pins and a real browser audio-graph run for each action

impact_assessment.why: beginDraft, undo, resetLevel and showHint all call audio.play('tick'), so the four most common loom actions sound identical and the only feedback for a hint, an undo or a reset is the same 35ms 660Hz blip.
impact_assessment.benefits: Each action gains a recognizable short signature without files, dependencies or new settings, and the existing mute toggle still silences all of them.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CUES gains three named cues and four app call sites change; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Frequency-pinned unit tests plus a browser probe that intercepts createOscillator for hint/undo/reset, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood, explicit staging, no push

[1/4] Cycle 7: make the skip link the first Tab stop on initial load and make <main> focusable, so keyboard users can jump past the title art; prove with a 1440x900 Tab-focus before/after pair and a dogfood Tab-Enter-Tab keyboard run

impact_assessment.why: Boot calls setScreen('title'), which focuses the h1, so the first Tab lands on Play and never reaches the Skip to content link; the skip target <main id='main'> also has no tabindex, so even activating the link cannot move focus into the content.
impact_assessment.benefits: Keyboard users get a working first-stop skip link on every initial screen, later SPA screen changes still focus their headings, and no layout or game rule changes.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: setScreen initial-focus guard and main focus target; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first dogfood keyboard sequence (Tab reveals skip link, Enter focuses main, next Tab reaches Play), 1440x900 before/after focused-state pair, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood, explicit staging, no push

checkpoints.description: [1/4] Cycle 8: stop a ?daily=<past-date> deep link from opening and recording a historical daily, which back-fills a missed day and contradicts ADR-011; clamp every daily open to the local today, prove with a same-URL date before/after pair and a dogfood past-link run plus a solved-save key check

impact_assessment.why: A played ?daily=2026-11-06 run loaded 6 Kas 2026, solved it, saved days['2026-11-06'], and the levels history showed yesterday solved with a 1-day streak while today was missed; ADR-011 and README say a missed daily cannot be back-filled.
impact_assessment.benefits: The daily history and streak stay an honest record of days actually played, a shared past link cannot rewrite them, and today's daily remains the only writable daily.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: daily boot parameter and openDaily key; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: no save-schema change, but no past day can be recorded from the UI
impact_assessment.mitigation: Pure currentDailyKey helper with unit cases, failing-first dogfood past-link check, same-URL 1440x900 date pair, scratch before/after solves with saved-key report, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood, explicit staging, no push

[1/4] Cycle 9: rebalance the two 8x8 Act I outliers (Warp Song 24/64 and Shuttle 31/64) with the existing even cut, so no thread on a large loom swallows a third of the board; pin the invariant in tests, prove with a solved-board before/after pair and real plays of Shuttle

impact_assessment.why: Shuttle's longest solution thread is 31 of 64 cells (48%) and Warp Song's is 24 (38%), while every 8x8-or-larger chamber from Tapestry onward stays under a third; the giant thread makes most of the board one colour and the played route a long snake.
impact_assessment.benefits: Thread effort is distributed across the seven pairs, the board reads as a balanced weave, and the existing even-cut generator plus frozen-solution tests already support it; no rule, save or UI change.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: levels.js solutions for warp-song and shuttle; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: ids and save schema unchanged, stored best times remain but refer to the refreshed puzzles
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first balance test over every large chamber, regenerate only the two specs and diff the rest, validate all 24 solutions and totals, before/after solved-board pair plus real plays, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood, explicit staging, no push

[1/4] Cycle 10: preserve the chamber-index scroll position and focus when returning from a chamber, so a player who opens a late campaign card lands back on it instead of the top; prove with a seeded late-campaign 390x844 before/after pair and a dogfood scroll-return run

impact_assessment.why: The index renders 24 cards and setScreen always scrolls to the top; a returning player with 12+ chambers solved must scroll past a dozen cards again after every visit, especially on the single-column 390px layout.
impact_assessment.benefits: The index behaves like a persistent campaign map, the card you opened is focused and visible on return, and no save, engine or card-layout change is needed.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: openBoard/showLevels scroll and focus state; dependency: none; concurrency: single writer on a clean weft tree; state: in-memory scroll/focus only, no save change
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first dogfood seeded late-campaign scroll/return check, same-save 390x844 before/after pair, full npm test plus aikit check and dogfood, explicit staging, no push
